commands.short: Test known weak/compromised SSH keys against targets
commands.example:
# Single target
  brutus badkeys --target 192.168.1.10:22

  # Targets file (auto-fingerprinted, only SSH services tested)
  brutus badkeys --targets-file targets.txt

  # Pipeline mode
  naabu -host 10.0.0.0/24 -p 22 -silent | nerva --json | brutus badkeys

  # Pipe plain targets
  echo "192.168.1.10:22" | brutus badkeys

  # URI format
  echo "ssh://192.168.1.10:22" | brutus badkeys

  # Import targets from nmap XML scan (only SSH services tested)
  brutus badkeys --nmap-file scan.xml

commands.short: Test default credentials on non-HTTP services (SSH, databases, SMB, etc.)
commands.example:
# Single target
  brutus creds --target 192.168.1.10:22 --protocol ssh -p "password,Password1"

  # Pre-paired user:pass combos (no Cartesian product)
  brutus creds --target 10.0.0.50:22 -c "admin:admin,root:toor,deploy:deploy123"

  # Credentials file (user:pass per line)
  brutus creds --target 10.0.0.50:3306 -C creds.txt

  # Targets file (auto-fingerprinted with Nerva)
  brutus creds --targets-file targets.txt -u admin -P passwords.txt

  # Pipeline mode with Nerva JSON (HTTP and SNMP services are skipped)
  naabu -host 10.0.0.0/24 -silent | nerva --json | brutus creds -P passwords.txt

  # Pipe URI targets (protocol from scheme, no fingerprinting needed)
  echo "ssh://192.168.1.10:22" | brutus creds -p "password,Password1"

  # Import targets from nmap XML scan
  brutus creds --nmap-file scan.xml -P passwords.txt

  # Import targets from masscan (requires --protocol or auto-fingerprints with Nerva)
  brutus creds --masscan-file scan.json --protocol ssh -P passwords.txt

commands.short: Enumerate GitHub accounts by email (existence + username reveal)
commands.example:
# Existence-only enumeration (unauthenticated)
  brutus enum active github -e alice@example.com,bob@example.com

  # Generate candidate emails for a domain and enumerate the 5000 most likely
  brutus enum active github --domain target.com --format first.last --limit 5000

  # Enumerate emails from a file
  brutus enum active github -E emails.txt

  # Reveal usernames for existing accounts (requires a PAT with repo+delete_repo)
  export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...
  brutus enum active github -E emails.txt

  # Pace requests to avoid GitHub's existence-endpoint rate limiting
  brutus enum active github -E emails.txt --threads 2 --rate-limit 1

flags.name: credentials
flags.usage: Comma-separated user:pass pairs (e.g., admin:admin,root:toor)

flags.name: credentials-file
flags.usage: Credentials file (user:pass per line)

flags.name: experimental-ai
flags.usage: Enable AI-powered credential detection and Vision verification

flags.name: https
flags.usage: Use HTTPS for browser connections

flags.name: jitter
flags.usage: Random delay variance for rate limiting

flags.name: json
flags.usage: JSON output format

flags.name: masscan-file
flags.usage: Masscan JSON file (-oJ output) to import targets from

flags.name: mode
flags.usage: Aggressiveness tier: cautious, default, aggressive

flags.name: nmap-file
flags.usage: Nmap XML file (-oX output) to import targets from

flags.name: no-color
flags.usage: Disable colored output

flags.name: output
flags.usage: Output file for JSON results (implies --json)

flags.name: protocol
flags.usage: Protocol override (http or https)

flags.name: proxy
flags.usage: Proxy URL. HTTP enum sources accept http, https, socks5, socks5h (a bare host:port defaults to http, like curl); raw-TCP scan plugins support socks5/socks5h only. Examples: --proxy http://host:8080, --proxy socks5://127.0.0.1:1080

flags.name: proxy-user
flags.usage: Proxy credentials as user:pass (curl-style); takes precedence over credentials embedded in --proxy. Note: visible in process args/shell history.

flags.name: quiet
flags.usage: Quiet mode - only show successful credentials

flags.name: rate-limit
flags.usage: Max requests per second (0 = unlimited)

flags.name: retries
flags.usage: Max retries on connection error (0 = disabled)

flags.name: target
flags.usage: Target host:port

flags.name: targets-file
flags.usage: File of targets to test, one host:port per line (fingerprints with Nerva unless --protocol is set)

flags.name: threads
flags.usage: Number of concurrent threads

flags.name: timeout
flags.usage: Per-target timeout

flags.name: verbose
flags.usage: Verbose mode - show detailed progress to stderr

flags.name: verify
flags.usage: Require strict TLS certificate verification
